shorts.title: What you will learn: shared_ptr and weak_ptr
shorts.hook: Many owners, one object, deleted exactly once.
shorts.script: Many owners, one object, deleted exactly once. Today the ownership is shared. Many pointers own one object, and the last one to leave switches off the light. A shared pointer lets many owners share one object. A counter inside tracks the owners. When the last owner dies, the object is deleted. A weak pointer looks at the object but does not own it. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: shared_ptr and weak_ptr.

shorts.title: shared_ptr and weak_ptr in one minute
shorts.hook: A shared pointer lets many owners share one object.
shorts.script: A shared pointer lets many owners share one object. A counter inside tracks the owners. When the last owner dies, the object is deleted. A weak pointer looks at the object but does not own it. It does not change the counter. Think of a Wi-Fi password. Many people share it, and the router stays on until the last person leaves. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.script: W is a weak pointer. It owns nothing. S owns an int with the value seven. W now watches the same object. Expired asks if the object is gone. Not yet, so zero. Lock gives a shared pointer, if the object is alive. It reads seven. After the block, s is dead. The object is deleted, and expired is one. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A raw pointer into a shared_ptr
shorts.script: Bug of the Day. We assign a raw new result to a shared pointer. The compiler says it cannot convert int star to shared pointer. Use make shared instead. It builds the object and the counter in one safe step. The shared pointer constructor from a raw pointer is explicit, so an equals sign does not work. Make shared is also faster and safer. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Shared pointers are polite. The last one out always turns off the light.
shorts.script: Shared pointers are polite. The last one out always turns off the light. Make a shared pointer to an int. Copy it into a second shared pointer. Print use count. Write your answer in the comments. Many shared pointers can own one object. A counter tracks the owners, and the last owner deletes the object. A weak pointer watches without owning. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
